chunks: And Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about that amount of buried treasure for which khums becomes obligatory, so he said: “Whatever amount whose like is subject to zakat, then khums is due in it.”

key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: the obligatory alms-tax used here as a benchmark threshold
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth tax due on certain forms of wealth
key_terms.الْكَنْزِ: buried treasure or discovered hoarded wealth
key_terms.مِثْلِهِ: its equivalent, meaning an equivalent amount or measure

ai.seo_question: What amount of buried treasure makes khums obligatory according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the threshold of khums on buried treasure. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that the amount of treasure upon which khums becomes obligatory is determined by the equivalent amount that would make zakat obligatory.
